As explained in item 12 of WELSPECS , the hydrostatic heads calculated using segmented densities in the wellbore are damped to reduce the likelihood of stability problems. This is done by combining values from the previous timestep with those of the current timestep in a weighted average. An error has been identified in the implementation of this damping which meant that more damping was being applied than intended. This error has been fixed in the 2010.1 version of the simulator but has not been made the default behavior as it may result in changes in simulation results. The correct damping can be applied by setting this item to a non-zero value.
If set to a non-zero value, fluid in place reports and pressure averages include contributions from excavated blocks.

If set to a non-zero value, the pre-2010.1 behavior is restored for relative permeability interpolation based on capillary number in the Surfactant Model. For the 2010.1 version onwards the interpolation between immiscible and miscible relative permeability curves is only performed for blocks with a non-zero surfactant concentration. The immiscible curves are used for blocks with a zero surfactant concentration.
If set to a non-zero value, the pre-2010.1 behavior of river infiltration equations in the unsaturated regime is restored.

If set to a non-zero value, the pre-2010.1 behavior is restored for solving tracers in combination with multisegment wells (MSWs). For the 2010.1 version onwards, an error has been fixed in the coupled iterative solution of the tracers which previously led to wrong tracer rates and concentrations in the MSW segments. The change affects single phase, two phase and partitioned tracers.

If set to a non-zero value, the pre-2010.1 behavior is restored for GECON item 8. For the 2010.1 version onwards, the simulation will not be stopped if a group includes a follow-on well due to be opened in the next timestep.

If set to a non-zero value, the pre-2010.1 behavior is restored for calculating pinchout transmissibility values when item 4 of the PINCH keyword is set to ALL . This had an effect only in the 2010.1 and 2010.2 releases. From 2011.1 onwards the pre-2010.1 behavior has been restored unconditionally.

If set to a non-zero value, the pre-2010.1 behavior for the RPTRST argument RFIP is restored. The pre-2010.1 behavior calculated reservoir fluid-in-place to be surface fluid-in-place multiplied by formation volume factor. From 2010.1 this is calculated as pore volume multiplied by saturation.
Reserved.

parameters.brief: If set to 2, the pre-2016.1 behavior of the tracer-tracking option for VAPOIL and/or DISGAS cases with oil or gas phase tracers is activated
parameters.name: If set to 1, the pre-2011.1 behavior of the tracer-tracking option ( TRACERS ) is activated. This affects how the injected concentration for crossflowing wells is calculated.
This item relates to protection against bad cross-processor NNC set-up

If set to 2, all the effects of setting to 1 are introduced. Furthermore, the pre-2010.2 behavior regarding NNCs spanning multiple processors in parallel is restored. This behavior is known to be problematic in certain cases.
If set to a non-zero value, the pre-2010.2 method for end-point scaling is used with the minimum oil saturation tables ( SOMGAS or SOMWAT ).

If set to 1, the pre-2011.1 handling of SUMMARY keywords AAQR , AAQT , ALQR and ALQT is restored. Before 2011.1, the list associated with these keywords could contain an element referring to a gas analytic aquifer. If the list was empty, all analytic aquifers including gas one were listed. From the 2011.1 version on, using these keywords with a gas analytic aquifer is not allowed. Additionally, the ALL summary keyword implies the keywords AAQRG and AAQTG .

If set to 1, the phase saturations and oil-gas ratios are limited to explicitly bounded values. It is possible for a non-linear iteration to produce saturation values that are outside the physical range between 0.0 and 1.0. Usually the amount by which they are outside this range is small, but to prevent any problems with physical correlations, setting this option to 1 forces all saturations (for water, gas, oil and solvent) to be zero if less than zero, and to be one if greater than one, at the end of each non-linear iteration. Similarly, oil-gas ratios will be forced to zero if they are negative.
Reserved.

This item relates to changes to looped MSWs and ICDs. Pre-2011.1 behavior may be obtained by setting this item to 42 (that is the first, second and fourth bullet points below). The item has the following behavior:
If set to a multiple of 3, the pre-2011.1 behavior of item 6 of WSEGSOLV is restored. This affects the range of linearization for ICDs, AICDs, labyrinth devices and valves in looped MSWs.
If set to a multiple of 5, an alternative MSW linearization is applied for looped wells for high segment flow rates.
If set to a multiple of 7, the pre-2011.1 ICD solver implementation is restored.

parameters.brief: If set to 2, the 2011.1 miscible viscosity and density calculations are restored.
parameters.name: If set to 1, the pre-2011.1 miscible viscosity and density calculations are restored.

If set to 1, the pre-2011.1 behavior is restored for the reporting of the scaled table end-points in the debug file when EPSDBGS or EPSDEBUG is specified. For the 2011.1 version the scaled values are reported when no scaling is applied.
If set to 1, duplicated records in the FAULTS keyword are ignored. If a fault is specified twice, any multipliers associated with it are applied twice.

If set to 1, the pre-2011.1 behavior is restored when reading the SURFVISC keyword. From 2011.1 onwards the water viscosity in SURFVISC at zero surfactant concentration and reference pressure must be equal to the value entered in the PVTW keyword.

If set to 1, the pre-2011.1 behavior for initial tracer concentrations in cells containing no host phase is restored. This switch also activates equivalent behavior for the initial concentrations of surfactant, foam and polymer.

If set to a 1, the pre-2011.1 behavior is restored for the modeling of the two-phase relative permeability of oil to gas when using the EHYSTR or EHYSTRR keywords with item 2 set to 4 (Killough hysteresis applied to both wetting and non-wetting phases). In some cases it has been found that the two-phase relative permeability of oil to gas can exceed the maximum value specified in the drainage and imbibition oil saturation function tables, or the maximum value specified via the end-point scaling keywords KRO and IKRO (and their directional and irreversible variants) if ENDSCALE has been specified. Depending upon the choice of three-phase relative permeability model, this can result in the three-phase oil relative permeability also exceeding the maximum value from the tables or end-points. This has been addressed for the 2011.1 version by constraining the maximum value of the two-phase relative permeability of oil to gas to the maximum of the values specified in the drainage or imbibition tables, or end-points. The two-phase oil relative permeability of oil to gas is combined with the two-phase oil relative permeability of oil to water to form the three-phase oil relative permeability. The constraint described here, therefore, will apply to all three-phase oil relative permeability models available in ECLIPSE 100.
Reserved.
If set to 1, the pre-2011.1 behavior of WDFACCOR is recovered. This changes D-factor calculations for flow-dependent skin factor if fewer than 3 phases are present in reservoir.

If set to 1, the pre-2011.1 behavior is restored for the treatment of the NOHYST keyword. Prior to 2011.1, hysteresis was not deselected by this keyword if specified after the SATOPTS keyword or if WAG hysteresis was specified via the WAGHYSTR keyword.

If set to 1, this deactivates the processing of the ACTNUM data specified in an EGRID file identified by the GDFILE keyword. Note that in previous versions, the default was not to process ACTNUM ; from 2011.1, processing ACTNUM is the default.

If set to a negative value, the threshold tolerance for the adsorption calculation when using the cascade tracer solver is changed. The threshold tolerance affects the adsorption by skipping the calculation in cells where the amount of tracer and the rock mass is less than the threshold value. Item 171 can be used to control the threshold value. If set to a negative value, the threshold value is taken as 10 N where N is the value specified in item 171. The default value is 10 -12 . The pre-2011.1 value can be restored by setting N to -6. This option affects active tracers, such as surfactant, alkaline and foam, as well as environmental tracers solved by the cascade method.
If set to 1, the pre-2011.1 behavior of GSSCPTST is recovered. This affects simulations with local grid refinements.
If set to 1, the pressure is chopped if it falls below 1 atmosphere.

If set to 1, the pre-2011.1 behavior is restored for the treatment of the SWATINIT keyword when read via the IMPORT keyword. Prior to 2011.1, this method of reading the SWATINIT keyword resulted in some of the saturation table data consistency checks being omitted.
Reserved.
If set to 1 this reverts to pre-2012.1 behavior for polymer and brine in standard wells.
This option allows the use of the gradient option in parallel runs. This combination of features is unsupported and so should be used with caution as it may lead to unexpected results or errors.

If set to 1, the pre-2011.2 behavior for the processing of JFUNCR with hysteresis is restored. Prior to 2011.2 the per region processing of J-functions was only applied to the imbibition saturation tables for hysteretic models.

If set to 1, this restores the pre-2012.1 behavior for table look up for the coal bed methane option, using SATNUM and PVTNUM instead of COALNUM . This affect the keywords LANGMUIR , LANGSOLV , COALADS , COALPP and DIFFCOAL .
Not used.
This switch reverts part or all of the looped multisegment well (MSW) solver to the pre-2012.1 behavior.
If positive and divisible by 3, the predictor will not set every segment to a non-zero flow. This can lead to a singular well Jacobian and therefore problems with the well solution.
If positive and divisible by 5, the pre-2012.1 behavior of the tracer solver with looped multisegment wells is recovered. This behavior change can only be made in the RUNSPEC section.

When set to 1, this switch reverts the network balancing option to pre-2012.1 behavior. An additional check was added to the network balancing option to ensure that all well THP targets reflected their parent group’s node pressure. This check improves the accuracy of network balancing in certain circumstances such as when the reservoir coupling option is in use.
This switch reverts the behavior of hysteresis to pre-2012.1 behavior. It may affect two separate behaviors:

When set to a positive value divisible by 3, this switch reverts the calculation of critical gas saturation used to determine saturation chops to the pre-2012.1 behavior. Prior to 2012.1 the saturation curves were sometimes taken from the wrong region for this calculation.

This switch allows restarting from versions before 2012.1 if the combination of tracers with polymer or solvent or GI-condensate has been used. In this case, older versions of the code may have corrupted the data. Use of this switch is not recommended.

If set to 1, this switch reverts the WCONPROD and WCONINJE keywords to their pre-2012.1 behavior with respect to initialization for multisegment wells. Prior to 2012.1, any change of control mode by WCONPROD or WCONINJE caused the first guess of the well solution to be re-initialized. From 2012.1, this is not the case unless this option is set. This affects multisegment well convergence characteristics.

When set to 1, this switch reverts partitioned tracers to pre-2012.1 behavior. Prior to 2012.1, injecting connection flows of tracer were incorrectly calculated during the solving of the tracer equations.
Reserved.

When set to 1, this switch reverts the behavior of GSG non-neighbor connection and transmissibility allocation to pre-2012.1 behavior. This behavior in parallel can cause, in some situations, the non-neighbor connections and transmissibilities to be incorrectly communicated between processors.

If set to 1 (in the SOLUTION or earlier sections), the pre-2013.1 method of checking input enumerated saturation data is selected. For the 2013.1 version, the checking of input enumerated saturation data has been extended to check the data values against their expected end-points for end-point data derived both from saturation tables and end-point scaling arrays and tables.
This item has been deprecated. To control the number of messages output for dead block connections use item 13 of the MESSAGES keyword or OPTIONS item 220 .
This switch controls the number of warnings output regarding linear convergence problems. It can restore pre-2013.1 levels or suppress message output further.
If set to -1, it reduces messages regarding linear equation solver convergence problems further.
If set to 1, the pre-2013.1 behavior of approaching report steps will be active when using the ZIPPY2 keyword.
If set to 1, the pre-2012.2 behavior for assigning saturation end-points from end-point scaling arrays for two-phase models will be restored.
If set to 1, the pre-2012.2 behavior for a zero determinant detected in the linear solver is restored (stopping with an error). The new behavior is to chop the timestep and try to recover.

parameters.brief: If set to 1, the pre-2012.1 treatment of network choke branches will be used.
parameters.name: This option should not be needed in 2013.1 and later releases.

If set to 1, a modified WAG hysteresis gas relative permeability model will be used in situations where the transformed gas saturation at the start of the secondary or subsequent drainage cycle falls below the gas saturation at the start of the previous drainage cycle. This modification prevents excessive falls in gas relative permeability which can occur in such circumstances when the primary drainage curve is used to construct the secondary drainage cycle. More details are provided under "Hysteresis in WAG floods" in the ECLIPSE Technical Description .

If a well is set not to allow crossflow ( WELSPECS item 10) then, if there are convergence problems, this option will close any open connections that are trying to back flow and retry the well Newton iteration. This option should be set to the number of re-tries the simulator can perform before moving onto the next reservoir Newton iteration. The option is not enabled for multisegment wells.
If set to 1, the pre-2013.1 treatment of directional rock compression transmissibility multipliers will be used. This uses the x-direction multiplier for all NNCs.
If set to 1, the pre-2013.1 calculations for ROCKPAMA will be used. The derivative changes as specified in OPTIONS item 96 are ignored by default from 2013.1.

If set to 1, the additional WAG hysteresis regions specified via the WH2NUM and WH3NUM keywords and the associated additional processing (which applies whether these have been specified or defaulted) will be ignored. This should be specified in the RUNSPEC section. This option is only relevant when the WAGHYSTR keyword has been specified.
If set to 1, the pre-2013.1 version of the debug output for the scaled saturation tables specified via either the EPSDEBUG and EPSDBGS keywords will be selected.
If set to 1, this enables LGRs in USEFLUX runs where one or more parent cells are inactive because they lie outside the USEFLUX regions. Note that, by default, such LGRs are disabled.
If set to 1, the pre-2013.1 behavior is restored for the model initialization process for the case where item 2 of the EHYSTR keyword is set to -1.

If set to 1, connate gas will be included in the two-point scaling of the oil relative permeability to gas and water; that is, the maximum attainable oil saturation will be assumed to be constrained both by connate water and gas. By default, the connate gas is omitted from these calculations.
If set to 1, the pre-2013.1 behavior is restored for well connection ordering. This affects some cases with COMPORD and WRFT or WRFTPLT .

If set to 1, the pre-2013.1 behavior is restored for tracer calculations in cases with PARALLEL , VAPOIL , DISGAS and non-neighbor connections. It is recommended that you do not use this option as it recovers incorrect behavior in some cases.

If set to 1, the pre-2013.1 behavior is restored for error-checking of the second argument in keywords PLYVISCS , PLYVISCT and PLYVSCST . In particular, a lower bound of unity is now applied by default; activating this switch will allow any positive value.

If set to 1, the pre-2013.2 behavior is restored. The new, default behavior is to use the maximum adsorbed polymer concentration itself in a cell as the reference point for allowing (increasing adsorbate) or disallowing (decreasing adsorbate) changes in the adsorbed concentration. The previous behavior used the maximum solution polymer concentration as a proxy for this and did not take into account salinity changes.
If set to 1, the pre-2014.1 behavior is restored for the calculation of relative permeabilities when using the SURFACT or LOWSALT models with ENDSCALE .
If set to 1, the pre-2014.1 behavior is restored for the calculation of the capillary number when using the SURFACT and DUALPORO models.

parameters.brief: For the 2014.1 version, corrections have been made to the calculation of water relative permeability when subject to hysteresis and end-poin
parameters.name: If set to 1, the pre-2014.1 behavior is restored for the calculation of water relative permeability used as a component in the calculation of the three-phase oil relative permeability for Stone's Second Model STONE2 .
If set to 1, the pre-2014.1 behavior is restored for the calculation of the component cell heights for the GRAVDR model when used with either the SURFACT or LOWSALT models.

parameters.brief: If set to 2, unset values for all enumerated initial conditions in coarsened grids will be replaced with the value from an adjacent cell.
parameters.name: If set to 1, unset values for enumerated initial pressures in coarsened grids will be replaced with the value from an adjacent cell.
If set to 1, the error emitted in parallel when a well is defined using WELSPECL on an LGR that is switched off is downgraded to a warning.

If set to 1, the pre-2014.1 behavior for VDFLOW is restored such that the value of the inertial coefficient for non-Darcy flow is only applied to the first saturation region when more than one saturation regions have been defined. For the 2014.1 version, the inertial coefficient is applied to all saturation regions.

parameters.brief: For the 2014.1 version, by default, the non-Darcy flow component due to the VDFLOW or VDFLOWR keyword is not applied to the well connections
parameters.name: If set to 1, the pre-2014.1 behavior is restored for the non-Darcy flow component specified via the VDFLOW or VDFLOWR keyword. Prior to 2014.1 this was only applied to the phase mobility calculations for the well connections if the FHERCHBL keyword had also been specified.
If set to 1, the pre-2014.1 message output format for parallel runs is used; messages from slave processors will not appear in the output files for the master process.
If set to 1, the message output limit from MESSAGES item 13 is ignored.

parameters.brief: If set to 2, then the pre-2016.1 (but post 2014.1) behavior is restored.
parameters.name: If set to 1, the pre-2014.1 behavior for determining when a non-neighbor connection should be deleted based on its transmissibility is restored. Additionally, values which are below the cutoff value for all of transmissibility, diffusivity and thermal transmissibility will be preserved provided that the NNC itself is preserved. Note that, if this option is used, the diffusivity and thermal transmissibility settings from the MINNNCT keyword will have no effect.

If set to 1, the pre-2014.1 behavior for Killough hysteresis model for water wet systems will be selected. For the 2014.1 version, corrections have been made to the calculation of the wetting phase relative permeability when subject to hysteresis and end-point scaling.
If set to 1, more than one occurrence of the GRIDOPTS keyword is permitted.
If set to 1, the pre-2014.1 behavior for CECON is restored. UDAs used in CECON are applied to all connections in the wells specified with the particular UDA.

If set to 1, the pre-2014.1 versions of the LOWSALT and SURFACTW options are restored. The primary differences between the 2014.1 and pre-2014.1 versions relate to the modeling of end-point scaling when the ENDSCALE option has been specified. Prior to the 2014.1 version, end-point scaling was only applied to the high salinity end-points using SWL and associated keywords. For the 2014.1 version, end-point scaling has been added for:
for the high salinity (water-wet) saturation tables by introducing a new set of end-points including HWSWL
for the low-salinity (water-wet) saturation tables by introducing a new set of end-points including LWSWL

If set to 1, the effective well bore radius, used in the calculation of the well productivity index, can be greater than the drainage radius. Otherwise, the effective radius will be taken as the minimum of the effective radius and the drainage radius when calculating a well's productivity index. For the ECLIPSE 300 equivalent please refer to item 317 of the OPTIONS3 keyword.
If set to 1, the preferred phase of an injection well is not enforced to match the actual injection phase. For the ECLIPSE 300 equivalent please refer to item 318 of the OPTIONS3 keyword.

parameters.brief: If set to 2, this activates the pre-2014.1 conversion from velocity to shear rate and may only be applied to models that use keyword SHRATE
parameters.name: By default, prior to polymer shear calculations, ECLIPSE 100 now includes the mobile water saturation in the conversion from flow rate to velocity and, for runs including keyword SHRATE , applies a modified conversion factor from velocity to shear rate. If this item is set to 1, this activates the pre-2014.1 conversion from flow rate to velocity in which the mobile water saturation is excluded and may be applied to models that use either PLYSHEAR or PLYSHLOG .

If set to 1, the pre-2014.1 behavior for Killough hysteresis model for oil-wet systems will be selected. For the 2014.1 version, corrections have been made in the two phase oil to water relative permeability and connate water saturation was included in the calculation of oil to gas relative permeability.

If set to 1, the pre-2014.1 behavior of the 'TRNC' timestepping control for POLYMER / BRINE and SOLVENT runs will be restored. If set to 2, the 2014.1 behavior of the 'TRNC' timestepping control for POLYMER / BRINE runs will be restored.
If set to 1, the pre-2014.1 behavior of inverse lookup with three-point end-point scaling will be selected. For the 2014.1 version, corrections have been made in cases where SCALECRS is activated.

If set to 1, DUMPFLUX and USEFLUX may be used with various CEOR and tracer options which are normally banned in this combination. In this case, you must ensure that no CEOR or tracer effects occur outside the flux boundary.

If set to 1, the pre-2014.1 behavior for the input processing of the two-dimensional capillary pressure data specified via the PCG32D and PCW32D keywords will be restored. Prior to 2014.1, only the first table was used for all saturation regions. If more than table was specified, the second and subsequent tables were ignored. For the 2014.1 version, successive tables are read and allocated to their associated saturation regions.

If set to 1, the pre-2014.1 behavior for the scaling of gas relative permeability at residual saturation of the displacing phase ( KRGR ) for gas-water models with end-point scaling will be restored. Prior to the 2014.1 version, the residual saturation used to determine the gas relative permeability was calculated using the critical oil in water saturation. For the 2014.1 version, this is calculated using the critical water saturation.

If set to 1, the printed grid property tables in the PRT file will be scaled so that the maximum value in the table is always between 1 and 10. The units are appropriately rescaled to give the correct value overall. The default value of 0 gives the pre-2014.1 scaling, which only allowed certain rescaling magnitudes.

If set to 1, the pre-2014.1 geometry calculations are used to calculate neighbor transmissibilities for corner point geometry. Prior to the 2014.1 version, in some extreme cases (principally with a perfectly vertical fault which has cells on both sides sloping towards the fault) a small transmissibility value can be calculated between cells which are neighbors in i,j,k space even though the cells do not physically touch. When this switch is used, these cell indices and transmissibility values are also output to the debug file. Additionally, setting this switch to 1 reverts a similar issue with non-neighbour connections between an LGR and the adjacent global cell to the pre–2015.2 version of those calculations.

If set to 1, brine injection with the WSALT keyword may be used in dual porosity models with local grid refinements. This combination is banned otherwise. In this case you must ensure that the local grid properties do not differ from global cells.

If set to 1, the the pre-2014.1 behavior of the default interphase threshold pressure calculation will be activated. For the 2014.1 version, the interphase threshold pressure when defaulting item 3 of the THPRES keyword, will be calculated from the initial conditions considering any phase present in the upstream cell.

If set to 1, PVT extrapolation messages previously controlled by item item 94 of the OPTIONS keyword will be emitted. These messages are for oil/gas PVT extrapolation in a water-filled cell and extrapolation beyond the entered RS values in the oil pressure function look up.

If set to 1, the pre-2015.1 behavior is restored for the reporting of PCW and PCG and their imbibition counterparts and other variants in the PROPS section (via RPTPROPS ) when JFUNC or JFUNCR has been specified. For the 2015.1 version, these values are reported as capillary pressures by default or alternatively as J-Function scaling factors if this item is set to a value of 2. (Prior to the 2015.1 version, these values were reported as J-Function scaling factors for JFUNC and as default values for JFUNCR .)

If set to 1, the pre-2014.2 behavior is restored for the calculation of PCW and PCG (and their imbibition counterparts and other variants) in local grids when JFUNCR has been specified. For the 2014.2 version, these values are calculated according to the local grid properties and saturation functions. Prior to the 2014.2 version, these values were defaulted from the global grid.

If set to 1, the pre-2014.2 behavior is restored for the use of saturation functions when items 2 and 5 of the EHYSTR keyword are set to -1 and PC respectively. Prior to the 2014.2 version, if item 2 is set to -1, the drainage curves are used for equilibration and the imbibition curves are used for simulation if item 5 is set to BOTH or KR , but the drainage curves are used for both equilibration and simulation if item 5 is set to PC . For the 2014.2 version onwards, if item 2 is set to -1, the drainage curves are used for equilibration and the imbibition curves are used for simulation irrespective of the value assigned to item 5.

If set to 1, then where COORD or ZCORN values within an LGR do not align with the global grid values as required, they will be accepted and realigned with the global grid. This realignment only takes place for lines which are common to both grids - so if the LGR is significantly out of line, the geometry may still be invalid. This option is intended only to allow data sets to be run which are failing due to numerical rounding issues with very short LGR coordinate lines. If set to 2, then in addition to this, the pre-2015.1 tolerances used to determine whether an LGR's host cell has zero thickness are used.

If set to 1, the pre-2014.2 behavior for determining the threshold pressure of a fault ( THPRESFT ) through a non-neighbor connection is restored. Prior to the 2014.2 version, corrections were not made to the calculation of the fault threshold pressure to make it independent of the solver direction.

If set to 1 then, in models using corner point geometry, the pre-2014.2 calculation of global-local transmissibilities is restored in which the relevant cell transmissibilities are calculated internally rather than using values input via TRANX , TRANY and TRANZ .
Reserved.

If set to 1, pre-2015.1 behavior for MULTZ (and DIFFMZ if relevant) treatment in pinched-out columns is restored. If set to 2, 2015.x behavior is restored. If item 4 of the PINCH keyword is set to ALL, this affects the transmissibility of pinchouts which have different values of MULTZ for multiple inactive layers with non-zero pore volume within a pinchout. It is now felt that the pre-2015.x treatment of these cases is preferable, so it has been restored for 2016.1.
If set to 1, pre-2015.1 behavior is restored when the BHP is defaulted in the WCONINJP keyword.
Reserved.
If set to 1, pre-2015.1 values will be output for calculated rock volumes. This option is intended only for checking purposes. Simulation results are not affected.
Reserved.

If set to 1, then the pre-2014.2 behavior for directional transmissibility multipliers defined in the ROCKTABH keyword is restored. Use of this option is recommended only for back compatibility, as it can lead to the columns being interpreted as being in solver direction order rather than x, y, z order.

If set to 1, then the pre-2015.1 behavior for region set selection with data manipulation keywords such as EQUALREG is restored. If set to 2, then the pre-2020.2 behavior for source region set selection for OPERATE or OPERATER in the REGIONS section is restored. Use of this option is recommended only for back compatibility, as for some datasets it can lead to FLUXNUM being used as the region set when MULTNUM should be used.

If set to 1, ECLIPSE will use the pre-2015.1 calculation of well efficiency factor when making adjustments to take account of wells coming online when drilled after a delay due to keywords WDRILTIM or GRUPRIG , or ramping up when coming online due to a WTEST keyword.
If set to 1, ECLIPSE will use the pre-2015.1 algorithm for solving local grid refinements when using the CPR linear solver.
If set to ,1 ECLIPSE will not override the input value of NSTACK .

If set to 1, ECLIPSE will use new behavior following the problem concerning "UN-PHYSICAL” values from PVT tables messages. From 2015.1 onwards the new behavior using this switch is to immediately chop the timestep and advise that the PVT data be looked at. If the simulation is already at the minimum timestep the run will produce an error message.
The default wellbore volume for standard wells, see keyword WBOREVOL , can now be reduced by a factor of 10 OPTIONS(258) .
If set to 1, ECLIPSE will revert to the pre-2016.1 SMSPEC file structure. Prior to 2016.1 the INTEHEAD element of the SMSPEC file was not output.

If set to 1, the pre-2015.1 behavior will be restored for the treatment of connate gas in the end-point scaling calculations. For the current version, by default, connate gas is included in all end-point scaling calculations. Prior to the 2015.1 version, by default, connate gas was omitted from the end-point scaling calculations applied to the maximum oil saturation for oil relative permeability to water and gas when two-point scaling is specified ( SCALECRS not specified or specified with item 1 set to NO ) and for water relative permeability at residual oil saturation when three-point scaling is specified ( SCALECRS specified with item 1 set to YES ). For the current version, the functions of OPTIONS items 205 and 212 have been superseded. In addition, connate gas is now included in the end-point scaling of the relative permeability of oil to gas and water for the LOWSALT and SURFACT options. Previously this was not included when OPTIONS item 205 was set to 1.

If set to 1, this triggers the pre-2015.1 behavior for the Newton iteration solution update in POLYMER flood models with adsorption. This is done by deactivating a bisection algorithm (the algorithm is otherwise applied to deal with a particular type of convergence problem caused by an oscillation between two distinct intervals in the adsorption data supplied by either PLYADS or PLYADSS ).

If set to 1, pre-2015.1 behavior is used when a UDA is used for the artificial lift quantity (argument 8) in the WSEGTABL keyword. This option is intended for back compatibility purposes only, as it can result in the artificial lift quantity not being updated as expected, or being applied for all segments in a well when it was only specified for some of them.

If set to 1, pre-2015.1 behavior is used when the GRAVDRM keyword is used. This option is intended for back compatibility purposes only, as it can result in non-dual porosity non-neighbor connections having dual porosity settings applied to them when calculating flow.

If set to 1, the pre-2015.1 method is used to generate geometry-based NNCs in dual and multi-porosity models. This can result in connections being made between different porosities when the PINCHXY keyword is used. The new method is also more efficient when generating fault NNCs in dual porosity decks which are not dual permeability.

If set to 1, pre-2015.1 behavior is used when setting up NNC handedness in parallel. This option is intended for back compatibility purposes only as it can result in differences between serial and parallel in some parallel decks which include NNCs.

If set to 1, an alternative algorithm for generating x or y pinchouts is used. For complex geometry, for instance where pinchouts are needed across faults or where layers are extremely slanted or twisted, this can produce better results than the default algorithm. However, it may be better to use a specialist gridding package to generate these NNCs.

This item is meant for back-compatibility purposes only and its general use is strongly discouraged. If set to 1, the memory allocation algorithm for LGRs is reverted to the pre-2015.1 method. This will use less memory than in 2015.1 but may lead to unexpected behavior or numerical errors.
If set to 1, pre-2015.1 behavior is used for generating pinch connections when the cell pore volumes are modified in the EDIT section. This only affects parallel simulations.

If set to 1, pre-2015.1 capillary number calculations for the surfactant model in local grid cells are restored. This item is intended for back compatibility purposes only as the 2015.1 calculations are more robust. See "Surfactant model" in the ECLIPSE Technical Description .
Reserved.
If set to 1, pre-2015.1 behavior for NNCs in completed radial grids will be used (see keyword COORDSYS ).
If set to 1, pre-2015.1 treatment of NNCs with zero values for area multiplied by porosity will be used in polymer shear calculations.
If set to 1, pre-2015.1 treatment of non-directional NNC transmissibility will be used.
If set to 1, pre-2016.1 behavior for the checking of the end-point scaling keywords will be restored.
If set to 1, LGRCOPY is not banned in parallel runs. This may lead to incorrect behavior in cases where the LGR cells are not on the same processor as their host cells.
If set to 1, the pre-2016.1 API calculation will be used in sector runs with pressure boundary conditions.

If set to 1, the pre-2016.1 AICD segment strength calculation for both summary keyword SSTR and SEGSSTR output in the RFT file will be enabled. If set to 2, then this calculation is enabled only for SEGSSTR output in the RFT file.
If set to 1, additional messages about changes in well status will not be added to the PRT file (or the Event Reporter database file, if it is generated. See MESSSRVC ) .

If set to 1, then whenever the CSKIN keyword is specified or the value updated with a UDA, the reference value used in calculating the connection transmissibility factor for certain model types is also updated. This was the default behavior in ECLIPSE prior to 2016.1. If set to 2, the reference value is not updated. This was the default behavior in ECLIPSE 2016.x and 2017.x. For both values 1 and 2, the recalculated transmissibility factor is affected by non-permanent changes due to rock crushing tables, PI multiplier tables, or scale deposition. From 2018.1 onwards, non-permanent changes affect the connection transmissibility factor only on the relevant timestep.
If set to 1, the 2015.1 behavior for API and restarts will be enabled.

If set to 1, the mobile OIIP calculation used for FIP reports and some oil recovery efficiency summary vectors will be altered. Any changes to the pore volumes as applied by the ROCK / ROCKTAB family of keywords will not be applied to the mobile OIIP calculation, and instead the pore volumes at reference pressure will be used. This was the default behavior in ECLIPSE prior to 2016.1.

If set to 1, the pre-2016.1 calculation of NNC areas is used. Prior to 2016.1, some areas were always set to zero in coarsened grids, and this could lead to inaccurate velocity calculations. Use of this option switch is not recommended except for back compatibility purposes.
If set to 1, the pre-2016.1 limits for extreme capillary pressure values generated by the JFUNC and JFUNCR keywords are used. The new limits are more compatible with those used by E300.
If set to 1, the pre-2017.1 treatment of diffusivity in in-line NNCs for the coal bed methane model is used. The new treatment is more consistent with neighbour connections and non-inlined NNCs.

If set to 1, then the pre-2016.1 method of processing ADDZCORN and EQLZCORN in columns where only some of the cells have discontinuous surfaces will be used. Where arguments 8–11 are set to maintain continuous surfaces, then this will be applied even if only one side of a cell is continuous and the modification results in the top of the cell being below the bottom. This will produce geometry errors as these cells will then have negative DZ. The default behavior from 2016.1 is for no modifications due to these keywords to be carried out on a cell where they would result in the top corner being below the bottom corner.

If set to 1, an alternative method of calculating the contact area between active cells on either side of a pinchout is used. This will only have an effect if item 4 of the PINCH keyword is set to TOPBOT.

If set to 1, the pre-2016.1 behavior of the cascade tracer solver is restored for surfactant with alkali and reversible adsorption. This restores a bounds check on the surfactant concentration and may lead to material balance errors in cases where surfactant adsorption drops rapidly in response to alkali injection.

If set to 1, the pre-2016.1 behavior of the COMPORD keyword will be restored, where, if the second argument is set to INPUT, and the well crosses a parallel domain boundary, the connection order will not be honored.

If set to 1, then if the ADSALNOD and PLYADSS keywords or the SALTNODE and PLYVISCS keywords have a mismatch in the number of entries it is treated as a warning rather than an error. Use of this option switch is not recommended except for back compatibility purposes.

If set to 1, the pre-2016.1 behavior of item 3 of the WVFPEXP keyword will be restored, where a well which is not operating on the stabilized part of its VFP curve may be shut even if it is not currently under THP control.

If set to 1, the pre-2017.1 algorithm for upscaling the TOPS property in coarsened grid blocks will be restored. The old algorithm takes into account the value of TOPS for layers within each coarse cell other than the top one, and can result in a coarse cell having a TOPS value which is at a greater depth than any of the fine cells in its top layer. Additionally, in 2017.1 improvements have been made to the transmissibility upscaling for extreme geometry involving pinchouts and faults, and dual porosity, and setting this option switch to 1 will revert to the old behavior.

If set to 1, the pre-2016.2 algorithm for connection ordering is used. This only differs from the default algorithm for cases using the DUALPERM keyword where one or more wells is using the TRACK option for connection ordering, either by using the COMPORD keyword or by default. The TRACK option is only used if the well has one or more connections with a penetration direction of X or Y . The 2016.2 algorithm will place matrix and fracture connections adjacent to one another.

If set to 1, the pre-2017.1 algorithm for the depths used in fine scale equilibration is used. If set to -1, then the algorithm which was the default in 2017.x is used. The 2017 algorithm can be more robust in cases where either the pore-volume averaged depth (for coarsened grid blocks) or the user-specified depth is not in the vertical centre of the grid block and the gas-oil or gas-water contact is very close to the top or bottom of the grid block. For many cases the pre 2017 and 2018 behavior is identical, but for the 2018 algorithm, numerical aquifer blocks use the depth from the AQUNUM keyword and behave as if item 9 of the EQUIL keyword is set to 0.

If set to 1, ECLIPSE 300 values of surface mass density of air and pure water at standard conditions are used in the ECLIPSE 100 computations, see Table Constants used in the four unit conventions in the ECLIPSE Technical Description for more details.

If set to 1, the pre-2017.1 method for determining whether aquifer connections are allowed to a particular face of a local grid block when processing the AQANCONL keyword is used. This can lead to connections being made which would not exist for the equivalent geometry in a global grid.

If set to 1, the pre-2017.1 behavior for modifying connections which are located in coarsened blocks is restored. The new algorithm will apply modifications to connections which no longer match the coordinates specified in the keyword because they have been moved to the representative cell, while the old algorithm will not identify these as matches. Keywords affected are COMPRP , COMPIMB , COMPLUMP , COMPFLSH , COMPINJK , CECONT , WELOPEN , WINJMULT , WPIMULT and WSCCLEAN .
If set to 1, ECLIPSE will use the pre-2017.1 version of the CPR linear solver. This option switch applies to both ADAPTIVE mode and ORIGINAL mode.

If set to 1, ECLIPSE will use the pre-2017.1 implementation of GEFAC with the extended network solver. This affects how the efficiency factor is used when GEFAC item 3 is set to the default option of YES . From 2017.1 the efficiency factor is used when calculating pressure drops between the group specified and its parent node as well as pressure drops above the parent node; in previous releases the efficiency factor was only applied to pressure drop calculations above the parent node.

If set to 1, ECLIPSE will use the pre-2017.1 implementation of GCONPROD with of WCONHIST . Prior to 2017.1 some combinations of controls for these keywords led to well limits other than that set in item 3 of WCONHIST being imposed on wells controlled by both of these keywords.
If set to 1, ECLIPSE will use the pre-2017.1 implementation of items 4 and 6 of the WREGROUP . Prior to 2017.1, the test used included equality rather than being a strict inequality.
If set to 1, ECLIPSE will use the pre-2017.1 implementation of capillary pressure scanning curves.

If set to 1, ECLIPSE will use the pre-2017.1 method of calculating initial water saturation in cells where the gas-oil capillary pressure is non-zero: note this will result in the calculated initial water saturation not matching SWATINIT . From 2017.1 the gas-oil capillary pressure is included in the balancing calculations, and the initial water saturation will match SWATINIT .

If set to 1, ECLIPSE will use the pre-2017.1 implementation of velocity calculation at LGR boundaries. Velocity calculations are used in non-Newtonian flow calculations such as Forchheimer and Herschel-Bulkley. Prior to 2017.1 some of the connection and cell quantities stored at grid set up for use in velocity calculations were not stored correctly for a few connection types. Cell dimension in the connection direction and interface area were affected. If this option is set to 2 the pre-2017.1 storage of connection interface area will be recovered. If this option is set to 3 the pre-2017.1 storage of connection cell length will be recovered. If set to 1 then both are recovered.

If set to 1, ECLIPSE will use the pre-2017.1 method to calculate shear effects to polymer rheology at injecting well connections. Prior to 2017.1 the shear effects on connection fluid mobility were calculated using wellhead polymer concentrations. In some cases this led to anomalous transient increases in injectivity as other elements of the injection mobility are based on downstream properties. The 2017.1 method no longer shows these transient issues and has been found to converge more rapidly. This change affects cases with the PLYSHEAR or PLYSHLOG keywords.

If set to 1, the pre-2017.1 behaviour for leaving imbibition capillary pressure saturation curve unscaled, with SWATINIT data supplied in the capillary pressure hysteresis conditions, will be restored. The drainage capillary pressure curve is normally scaled as a consequence of SWATINIT application.

If set to 1, the pre-2017.1 behavior of the ACTION and ACTIONX keywords will be used. This facility has been added for back-compatibility and diagnostic purposes and is not recommended. Prior to 2017.1 the combination of these keywords with the GCONPRI , NETWORK or WRFTPLT keywords occasionally resulted in unintended behavior.

If set to 1, the pre-2018.1 behavior of the BVELxx and BSRTWx summary vectors with the ENDSCALE option active is restored. Their values are then calculated using the unscaled critical end-points. This does not match the internal simulator calculations and is intended for back-compatibility and diagnostic purposes only.
If set to 1, the pre-2018.1 memory allocation algorithm for local grids is used. In most cases this is a significant over-estimate and the new algorithm is much more efficient.

If set to 1, the pre-2018.1 behavior for SGWFN is restored, and values for the first item in column 2 and the last item in column 3 are allowed to be non-zero provided they have a magnitude smaller than 10 -6 .

If set to 1, the pre-2018.1 behavior for explicitly specified permeabilities in local grids for dual porosity or dual permeability cases is restored and values in the fracture will not be multiplied by the fracture porosity regardless of whether NODPPM is specified.
If set to 1, the pre-2018.1 behavior for LGRCOPY is restored and it will not be applied inside REFINE keywords in the GRID section unless explicitly specified inside the REFINE .

If set to 1, the pre-2018.1 behavior for AITS is restored. This may lead to report step times and dates in the SCHEDULE section not being respected if Reservoir Coupling, Open ECLIPSE or Gas Accounting are being used.

If set to 1, an alternative parallel transfer mode is used during the grid setup phase. This can be used to avoid problems in third party MPI libraries due to large data transfers. Results will not be changed by this option switch.

If set to 1, the pre-2018.2 behavior associated with a UDA in argument 6 or 7 of WCONPROD is restored. In versions prior to 2018.2, when the WELDRAW keyword is specified, the limit used in associated calculations will be the value of the UDA when the WCONPROD keyword was specified rather than the current value of the UDA.

If set to 1, the pre-2019.1 behavior for numerical aquifer connections in parallel is restored. Use of this switch is not recommended except for back compatibility checks, as it may lead to some connections not being made.

If set to 1, the pre-2019.1 behavior for autorefined grids in parallel is restored. Use of this switch is not recommended except for back compatibility checks, as it may lead to poor convergence and/or incorrect assignment of grid and aquifer properties to the refined grid. Serial behavior is unaffected and the new parallel behavior should be much more consistent with it.

If set to 1, the pre-2019.1 behavior for tracer tracking with LGRs using local timestepping in parallel is restored. Use of this switch is not recommended except for back compatibility checks, as it may lead to poor convergence, inaccurate results, and/or early run termination. Serial behavior is unaffected and the new parallel behavior should be much more consistent with it.

If set to 1, the pre-2019.1 solver setup for runs which are both a restart and use flux boundary conditions is restored. This can cause serious convergence issues which can then cause a difference in results, so use of this switch is not recommended except for back compatibility checks.

If set to 1, an alternative workflow for flexible restarts is activated. In this workflow, transmissibilities are not reloaded from the restart file, but are recomputed from the information in the dataset, including sequential application of transmissibility multipliers specified in the SCHEDULE section before the restart date. To give meaningful results, the SCHEDULE section must therefore be unchanged from the base case, with keyword skipping performed using SKIPREST . This workflow is not suitable for cases where transmissibility modifiers are applied conditionally, for instance using the ACTIONX keyword.

If set to 1, the pre-2019.2 behavior for non-Darcy flow is restored. From 2019.2, there have been improvements to the algorithm for the NNEWTF and VDFLOW keywords in dual porosity and/or rock compaction cases.
If set to 1, the pre-2019.2 behavior for WECON is restored. From 2019.2, negative contributions from crossflowing connections are included in the checks.

If set to 1, the pre-2019.2 behavior for surfactant in dual porosity models which use the GRAVDR keyword is restored. The 2019.2 algorithm has been improved to avoid a situation where either the run would fail or some grid blocks with a geometric non-neighbour connection could have their matrix-fracture potential difference set to 0. Use of this switch is not recommended except for back compatibility checks.

If set to 1, the pre-2019.2 behavior of the WTEST keyword is restored. The 2019.2 algorithm has been improved to avoid a situation where a problem in an already shut well's potential calculations could cause the testing interval to be extended.

If set to 1, the pre-2019.3 behavior for summary vectors associated with the GWRTWCV keyword is restored. For serial runs, the new behavior is unchanged except for cases where the well used as the gradient parameter has no open connections. For parallel runs, the new behavior is now consistent with the serial behavior. Use of this switch is not recommended except for back compatibility checks.

If set to 1, the pre-2016.1 behavior for the WELDRAW keyword with a UDA in item 2 is restored. This allows the UDA to turn the drawdown limit on and off if item 4 is set to NO, but does not function correctly if item 4 is set to YES.

If set to 1, the pre-2019.3 behavior for well and connection keywords which accept well lists or templates, or can be used with ? in an ACTIONX condition, is restored. From 2019.3, the default behavior is to give a warning and ignore the record if the set of wells it applies to is empty. Prior to 2019.3, if the record applied to no wells it was treated as an error.

If set to 1, the pre-2020.1 behavior for the TEMP keyword is restored. From 2020.1, a wide range of issues have been fixed, some of which could cause runs to fail. In particular, thermal conductivity calculations have been corrected for dual porosity single permeability cases, and rock volume calculations have been made compatible with ECLIPSE 300.
If set to 1, then for COAL cases, the pore volume averaged pressure excludes coal-filled cells.

If set to 1, the pre-2020.2 behavior for lift gas in extended networks is restored. When item 4 of NODEPROP is set to YES, the ALQ contribution for all production wells will be added to the network even if the well in question is shut or stopped.
If set to 1, the pre-2020.3 behavior for option 2 of the GASFDELC keyword is restored for extended networks. This may cause incorrect values to be reported for the gas delivery capacity.

If set to 1, an alternative method is used to calculate defaulted aquifer pressure for Carter-Tracy aquifers. This may put the aquifer in closer equilibrium with the grid in cases where the oil and water phase pressures are significantly different.

If set to 1, the pre-2021.1 behavior for connection ordering in restart files is restored. In some cases, this may lead to information being unavailable in restart runs, which can cause problems with functionality that depends on connection ordering (such as the output of PLT files and some options of the GECON keyword). Use of this switch is not recommended except for back compatibility checks.

If set to 1, the pre-2021.1 behavior for lumped completions is restored. This re-enables use of the COMPLUMP keyword for LGR wells that are not in amalgamated LGRs in parallel runs, but the lumped completions are not applied to any well in an LGR that is not hosted on processor 1, regardless of whether the lumped completions were specified with COMPLUMP or COMPLMPL .

This concerns the multisegment well model and controls how local mixture densities are used in segments that represent autonomous inflow control devices. For segments that contain such devices, an exponentiated mixture density is defined (see the WSEGAICD keyword for details) and used only as the density terms in the device's form pressure drop equation. A simple linear mixture density is used for the simulator’s internal conversion from mass to volumes rates as required by the form pressure drop equation. If this item is set to 1, the pre-2021.1 behavior is restored whereby the exponentiated mixture density is not only used where it is explicitly stated in the form pressure drop equation, but also in the conversion from mass to volumes rates.

If set to 1, the pre-2021.1 convention of limiting the PRT file width to 132 characters is restored. This disables the output of any new columns that would increase the width of a table beyond this limit.

If set to 1, the pre-2021.2 behavior for combining connection values using wildcard indices in UDQ functions is restored. If all three indices are specified, even if one or more of them is defaulted using -1, only the first match will be used in the function.

If set to 1, the pre-2021.2 memory management for the multisegment well model with local grid refinement is restored. This can use significantly more memory than the new system. It can also produce erroneous results if local grid summary vectors are used in ACTIONX conditions.

If set to 1, the pre-2021.4 behavior for circle completion in radial grids is restored. For single reservoir models, this can lead to the circle being completed on some layers of the grid and not others.

If set to 1, the pre-2022.1 behavior for global-local transmissibility calculations in cases where transmissibility values are supplied in the EDIT section is restored. Supplied values may not be correctly applied.

If set to 1, LGR transmissibility values supplied in the EDIT section for the positive face of a local grid will be used to calculate global-local transmissibilities. By default, these values are always taken to be zero, and specifying any value for them will cause the global-local transmissibility to be set to zero. This facility is available for Cartesian local grids using the NEWTRAN method only.

If set to 1, the pre-2022.2 validity checking for field summary keywords is restored. For some keywords, this will allow additional characters after the name, which may not be understood by some post-processors.
If set to 1, the pre-2022.2 validity checking for ACTIONX condition index values is restored. In some cases, an invalid or zero index will be treated as 1.

If set to 1, the pre-2022.3 limitations on group keyword UDAs (having to specify any UDA for the field after those for groups, and only being able to specify a UDA for one phase at a time) are restored.

OPTIONS3.description: The OPTIONS3 keyword can be used to activate special options within particular facilities in ECLIPSE 300. These options are mainly of a temporary or experimental nature, or act to restore back-compatibility with earlier versions of the code.
OPTIONS3.name: OPTIONS3
parameter_names: Set to 1 to obtain the explicit hydrostatic head values in the well model when the head calculation is based on an averaged wellbore density.
Set to 1 to obtain the FREEZEPC option. This will be overridden if the FREEZEPC , NOFREEZE or DPCDT keywords are used.
Set to 1 for saturation clipping.
New Material Balance Control on Convergence
Set to 1 to use a saturation pressure test to determine the phase in separator calculations.
With effect from the 2014.1 release, this item is no longer available.
Set to 1 to interpolate initial compositions from the constructed internal tables rather than directly from user-specified data.
Set to 1 to add the water-gas capillary pressure to the water phase rather than to the gas phase for the Gas-Water model.
Set to non-zero value to assign a zero THP for zero rate wells. Set to -1 to obtain the pre-2009.1 behavior for this option switch.
Controls output of VFP extrapolation messages
If > 0 potential reversal chops are switched on.
If > 0 the pre-98A equilibration method is used.
If > 0 the pre-98A average specific volume derivative is used to normalize the solution change reported in the non-linear iterations.
If > 0 the actual specific volume normalization is used instead of the average specific volume derivative in the non-linear iterations.
If > 0 the reference surface tension, if defaulted, is taken as the initial cell-by-cell values rather than the field average. This was the pre-98A behavior.
If > 0 use pre-98A constant slope extrapolation of K-values.
If = 1 switch off well BHP solution damping.
If = 1 disable the saturation-based Appleyard Chop for the Thermal option.
Turn off non-linear speed-up due to Gain.

When modeling oil-wet systems with the end point scaling option activated, it is advantageous to be able to scale the water-oil capillary pressure at the maximum water saturation (using keyword PCW ) rather than at the entry (connate) water saturation (where the water saturation equals SWLPC ). This switch caters for this situation. Of rather less interest, but for completeness, it is possible to scale the gas-oil capillary pressure (keyword PCG ) at connate rather than maximum gas saturation using this option switch. If OPTIONS3 (143) is non-zero and divisible by 2 then the water-oil capillary pressure is scaled at the maximum water saturation; and if OPTIONS3 (143) is non-zero and divisible by 3 then the gas-oil capillary pressure is scaled at the connate gas saturation. If OPTIONS3 (143) is set to 1, then any water capillary pressure curves for which P c o w is entirely positive are chosen as water-wet and scaled at the entry saturation SWLPC while any for which P c o w is entirely negative are scaled at the maximum saturation SWU . For mixed wettability curves, it would be a bit of an illusion to arbitrarily choose which end point to scale at, so setting this option switch to 1 does nothing for such curves. When the SWATINIT keyword is used to match an initial water distribution then the scaling on P c o w is more sensible if OPTIONS3 (143)=1 when the rocks are either water wet or oil wet (but no mixed wettability rocks). When the SWATINIT keyword is used to match an initial water distribution for mixed wettability rocks and positive capillary pressure dominated then the scaling on P c o w is more sensible if OPTIONS3 (143)=5 (minimum capillary pressure is fixed). When the SWATINIT keyword is used to match an initial water distribution for mixed wettability rocks and negative capillary pressure dominated then the scaling on P c o w is more sensible if OPTIONS3 (143)=7 (maximum capillary pressure is fixed). Note that OPTIONS3 (143)=5 and OPTIONS3 (143)=7 are not scaling the capillary pressure above GOC, therefore, SWATINIT cannot be honored above GOC.
