If set to 1, the pre-2021.3 behavior for well separators is restored. If the WELSPECS or WELSPECL keyword is respecified and connections added to the well without also respecifying the WSEPCOND keyword, new connections may not use the correct separator.
If set to 1, the pre-2021.3 behavior for the ZI keyword is restored. Initial calculations for dissolved hydrocarbons will be based on the calculated composition rather than the composition specified.

If set to 1, the pre-2021.3 behavior for the SECTOR keyword is restored. The non-neighbor connection data written to the grid and INIT files will have indexes based on the entire grid rather than the sector.

If set to 1, the pre-2021.3 behavior for the ROCKCONL keyword is restored. Specifying it before the related local grid has been defined will not be treated as an error. Connection indexes may be incomplete or incorrect.

If set to 1, alternative reporting for the ROPR , RGPR , ROPT and RGPT region summary keywords is enabled. The reported volumes will be calculated using the separator defined in the FIPSEP keyword, rather than using the well separator for each connection in the region.
Reserved for future development.

If set to 1, the pre-2021.4 behavior for parallel restart runs which also use a flux file is restored. For some geometries, properties from the restart file may not be assigned to the correct grid blocks. Use of this option is not recommended except to confirm the reason for a change in results.
If set to 1, the pre-2021.4 behavior for the MULTTHT keyword in the SCHEDULE section is restored. The transmissibility of circle completion non-neighbor connections will not be modified.
If set to 1, the pre-2022.1 behavior for the KVCRWAT keyword is restored. No checking is performed to ensure that the temperature in a calculation is greater than item 5.

If set to 1, the pre-2022.1 behavior for GASWAT and CO2STORE non thermal cases is restored. Injection wells under water rate control may inject at a much higher rate than requested and switch to BHP control.
If set to 1, the pre-2022.1 behavior for CO2STORE thermal cases with no hydrocarbon components is restored. The minimum reservoir temperature will be constrained to 10 °C rather than 1 °C.

If set to 1, the pre-2022.1 behavior for group rate and total reporting is restored. For complex multi-level group structures with rate controls low down the tree, group rates may not be correctly updated.

If set to 1, when solid mole fraction output is requested, it will be output for all components, including components which can never be in the solid phase. The default behavior is to produce output only for components which can exist in the solid phase unless (for BSMF and LBSMF ) a specific non-solid component is requested. Output will be produced in this case, but will always be zero.
If set to 1, the pre-2022.2 validity checking for ACTIONX index condition index values is restored. In some cases, an invalid or zero index will be treated as 1.

If set to 1, the pre-2022.3 limitations on group keyword UDAs (having to specify any UDA for the field after those for groups, and only being able to specify a UDA for one phase at a time) are restored.

If set to 1, the pre-2022.4 behavior for the IMPNOMFD option of the CO2ENTH keyword is restored. For high aqueous mole fractions of CO 2 , the aqueous enthalpy of CO 2 will have some mole fraction dependency.

If set to 1, the pre-2022.4 behavior for UDAs in the WCONPROD keyword is restored. Calculations for wells controlled by steam rate target, or using the thermal cutoff option, may not be identical to an equivalent model using UDAs in the WELTARG keyword, or keyword redefinition.
If set to 1, the pre-2022.4 timestepping behavior for the DELAYACT keyword is restored. If a delayed action is redefined after its controlling action has been triggered, timesteps may be very short.

If set to 1, the pre-2023.1 behavior for calculations when the CVTYPE or CVTYPES keyword is used is restored. Values dependent on the critical temperature (e.g. EOS density and LBC viscosity) will not use the user-supplied TCRIT values, and may be non-physical, as an extreme critical temperature is used for the GAS and DEAD phase options. Additionally, if CGVTYPE or COVTYPE is specified without a corresponding CGDTYPE or CODTYPE keyword, the viscosities may not be calculated correctly.

If set to 1, the pre-2023.1 internal upper pressure limit for well calculations when the CO2STORE keyword is used is restored. Some calculations may be performed at a pressure higher than the Spycher-Pruess limit of 600 bar for models where the pressure is within the limit.

The difference is that the PINCH keyword allows you to specify a maximum threshold thickness for pinched-out cells, whereas if you use the PINCHOUT keyword the threshold thickness is fixed at 0.001 (in all unit sets).
PINCHOUT.name: PINCHOUT

PINCHREG.description: This keyword supplies data for calculating pinchouts in multiple regions. The regions should be identified using keyword PINCHNUM . If PINCHNUM is not specified, then PINCHREG applies to flux regions defined by FLUXNUM . If neither PINCHNUM nor FLUXNUM is specified then PINCHREG is ignored.
PINCHREG.name: PINCHREG

PLMIXNUM.description: The PLMIXNUM keyword is used with the Polymer flooding option to define regions with different polymer characteristics. See keywords PLMIXPAR and PLYMAX . The keyword should be followed b

PLMIXPAR.description: This keyword should only be used in runs which use the polymer model (keyword POLYMER ).
PLMIXPAR.name: PLMIXPAR

If it is used, multiple adsorption tables can be used, with each table giving the adsorption data at one temperature. In this case, the keyword PLYATEMP is used to give the temperature value of the adsorption table which fo

parameters.name: Temperature.

PLYCAMAX.description: This keyword is optional, and is used to customize data for the Polymer Flood Model on a cell-by-cell basis. See "Polymer flood model" in the ECLIPSE Technical Description for further information.
PLYCAMAX.name: PLYCAMAX

PLYDHFLF.description: This keyword describes the thermal degradation of polymer due to temperature. The data comprises NTPVT (set in the TABDIMS keyword) tables of polymer thermal degradation functions, each terminated by a slash (/). Each table consists of the following columns of data:
PLYDHFLF.name: PLYDHFLF

The corresponding half-life of the polymer.

PLYESAL.description: This keyword may only be used when the multi-component brine model (keyword BRINE in conjunction with keyword ECLMC in the RUNSPEC section) is active in conjunction with the polymer option (keyword POLYMER in the RUNSPEC section).
PLYESAL.name: PLYESAL

PLYKRRF.description: This keyword is optional, and is used to customize data for the polymer flood model on a cell-by-cell basis. See "Polymer flood model" in the ECLIPSE Technical Description for further information.
PLYKRRF.name: PLYKRRF

PLYMAX.description: The data comprises NPLMIX (see item 10 in RUNSPEC keyword REGDIMS ) rows of maximum polymer and salt concentrations that are to be used in the mixing parameter calculation of the fluid component viscosities. Each table consists of the following items of data:
PLYMAX.name: PLYMAX
parameter_names: The value of the polymer concentration in the solution which is to be used in the calculation of the maximum polymer fluid component viscosity.

The value of the salt concentration in the solution which is to be used in the calculation of the maximum polymer fluid component viscosity. This item is ignored if the salt-sensitivity keyword BRINE is not specified in the RUNSPEC section.

parameters.name: The value of the salt concentration in the solution which is to be used in the calculation of the maximum polymer fluid component viscosity. This item is ignored if the salt-sensitivity keyword BRINE is not specified in the RUNSPEC section.

PLYOPTS.description: This keyword sets optional parameters for the ECLIPSE 300 polymer model. See the "Polymer flood model" in the ECLIPSE Technical Description for further information.

PLYRMDEN.description: This keyword is optional, and is used to customize data for the polymer flood model on a cell-by-cell basis. See "Polymer flood model" in the ECLIPSE Technical Description for further information.
PLYRMDEN.name: PLYRMDEN

PLYROCKM.name: PLYROCKM

PLYSHEAR.name: PLYSHEAR

The corresponding factor applied to the effective water and polymer viscosities (entered using PVTW with PLYVISC , PLYVISCS , PLYVISCT or PLYVSCST ) due to shear thinning/thickening of the polymer.

PLYSHLOG.description: This keyword is used to activate the alternative (logarithm-based) polymer shear thinning/thickening option and to supply the required shear effect data. The keyword is optional and, if omitted, no shear effect calculations are performed. This keyword therefore activates a variant of the polymer shear thinning/thickening model activated by keyword PLYSHEAR .

PLYTRRF.description: This keyword should only be used for polymer studies. It describes the temperature dependence of the residual resistance factor given by the second data item of keyword PLYROCK or by PLYKRRF .
PLYTRRF.name: PLYTRRF
parameter_names: Temperature.

The corresponding factor by which the residual resistance factor (entered using the PLYROCK or PLYKRRF keywords) has to be multiplied to give the temperature-dependent residual resistance factor of adsorbed polymer.

PLYVISC.description: The data comprises NTPVT (set in the TABDIMS keyword) tables of polymer viscosity multiplier functions, each terminated by a slash (/), describing the effect on the viscosity of pure water of increasing the concentration of polymer in solution. Each table consists of 2 columns of data:
PLYVISC.name: PLYVISC
parameter_names: The polymer concentration in the solution.

The corresponding factor by which the water viscosity (entered using the PVTW keyword in ECLIPSE 100 or the corresponding "Water components" keywords in ECLIPSE 300) has to be multiplied to give the viscosity of the solution.

PLYVISCS.description: This keyword should only be used for polymer studies when the salt- sensitivity option has been activated (in ECLIPSE 100 keyword BRINE in the RUNSPEC section without ECLMC , in ECLIPSE 300 the use of this keyword will activate the salt-sensitivity option).
PLYVISCS.name: PLYVISCS
parameter_names: The polymer concentration in the solution.

The corresponding factor by which the water viscosity (entered using the PVTW keyword in ECLIPSE 100 or the corresponding "Water components" keywords in ECLIPSE 300) has to be multiplied to give the viscosity of a fully mixed solution of polymer/salt at a polymer concentration given by item 1 and a salt concentration given by item 1 in the corresponding salinity table ( SALTNODE keyword in ECLIPSE 100 or ESPNODE keyword in ECLIPSE 300).

PLYVISCT.description: This keyword should only be used for polymer studies when the temperature option has been activated (keyword TEMP in the RUNSPEC section) and the salt-sensitivity option has not been activated (that is not using keyword BRINE in RUNSPEC ).
PLYVISCT.name: PLYVISCT
parameter_names: The polymer concentration in the solution.

The corresponding factor by which the water viscosity (entered using the PVTW keyword) has to be multiplied to give the viscosity of a fully mixed solution of polymer at a polymer concentration given by item 1 and a temperature given by item 1 in the corresponding TEMPNODE table.

PLYVSCST.description: This keyword is for polymer studies when the salt-sensitivity option has been activated (keyword BRINE in the RUNSPEC section) and when the temperature option has been activated (keyword TEMP in the RUNSPEC section). You use PLYVSCST with associated settings in keywords SALTNODE and TEMPNODE to specify a full three-dimensional polymer/salt solution/temperature viscosity function.
PLYVSCST.name: PLYVSCST

PMANUM.description: The keyword should be followed by one integer for every grid block in the current box specifying the pressure maintenance region to which it belongs. The region number should not be less than 1 or greater than the number of pressure maintenance tables, specified with TABDIMS .
PMANUM.name: PMANUM

PMAX.description: The keyword should be followed by some or all of the following items, indicating the maximum pressure likely to be reached during the simulation and additional information governing total compressibility checks. The record should be followed by a slash (/).
PMAX.name: PMAX
parameter_names: The maximum pressure likely to be reached during the simulation
Maximum pressure value to extend the range of pressures for checking total compressibility of the system.
Minimum pressure value to extend the lower range of pressures for checking total compressibility of the system.

parameters.name: Minimum pressure value to extend the lower range of pressures for checking total compressibility of the system.

PMISC.description: The PMISC keyword is optional, and may only be used in miscible runs (see keyword MISCIBLE ). It supplies tables that control the transition between immiscible and miscible displacement as a function of oil pressure. If this keyword is not present in miscible runs, miscible displacement is assumed to occur at all pressures; pressure having no effect on the miscibility. See "Miscible flood modeling
PMISC.name: PMISC
parameter_names: The local oil phase pressure.
The corresponding miscibility, on a scale from 0.0 to 1.0.

POLYMER.description: This keyword activates the Polymer Flood Model (see "Polymer flood model" in the ECLIPSE Technical Description ).
POLYMER.name: POLYMER

PORO.description: The keyword should be followed by one non-negative real number for every grid block in the current input box, specifying the fractional porosity value for each cell.
PORO.name: PORO

PORV.description: The keyword should be followed by one non-negative real number for every grid block in the current input box, specifying the grid block pore volumes.
PORV.name: PORV

PPCWMAX.description: This keyword can be used to limit the scaling of the capillary pressure curves when the SWATINIT keyword has been used to input an initial water distribution. Typically, if the input water saturation is above the connate saturation in blocks well above the transition zone, the scaling of the P c curve leads to unphysically high capillary pressure values.
PPCWMAX.name: PPCWMAX
parameter_names: The maximum capillary pressure for this saturation region; it must be greater than the maximum capillary pressure in the corresponding saturation function table.

PRCORR.description: This keyword requests that a slightly modified form of the Peng-Robinson equation of state is to be used, as described in "Equations of state" in the ECLIPSE Technical Description . This changes the usual form of the Ω a value as a function of the component acentric factor.
PRCORR.name: PRCORR

PREF.description: This keyword can only be used with the THERMAL option (keyword THERMAL in the RUNSPEC section).
PREF.name: PREF

PREFS.description: This keyword can only be used with the THERMAL option (keyword THERMAL in the RUNSPEC section).
PREFS.name: PREFS

PREFT.description: This keyword can only be used with the thermal option (keyword THERMAL in the RUNSPEC section).
PREFT.name: PREFT

PREFTS.description: This keyword can only be used with the thermal option (keyword THERMAL in the RUNSPEC section).
PREFTS.name: PREFTS

PREFW.description: PREFW specifies the reference pressure used in calculating the water density and water viscosity for each of the N w water components.
PREFW.name: PREFW

PREFWS.description: This optional keyword supplies reference pressures for water components for use in the surface calculations. The default, if it is not supplied, is for these to follow the reservoir values supplied with PREFW . If this keyword is supplied, the use of defaulted items is not allowed; values shall be input for each water component (see keyword COMPW ).
PREFWS.name: PREFWS

PRESSURE.description: The keyword should be followed by one real number for every grid block specifying the initial pressure. The data field should be terminated by a slash(/).
PRESSURE.name: PRESSURE

PRIORITY.description: This keyword is used to switch on the well prioritization option, and to set coefficients in the priority equations.
PRIORITY.name: PRIORITY

PROPS.description: The PROPS section of the input data contains pressure and saturation dependent properties of the reservoir fluids and rocks.
PROPS.name: PROPS

PROPS_END_POINT_SCALING.description: In some cases the relative permeability and capillary pressure tables vary from cell to cell. Rather than enter large numbers of tables it is possible to scale fixed points on a table to new cell-dependent positions. This may be done horizontally - along the saturation axis - or vertically - rescaling the values of K r and P c .
PROPS_END_POINT_SCALING.name: PROPS_END_POINT_SCALING

PROPS_FOAM_MODEL.description: This option is available in both simulators, though some keywords are only available in ECLIPSE 100.
PROPS_FOAM_MODEL.name: PROPS_FOAM_MODEL

PROPS_HYSTERESIS.description: If hysteresis is being used, both imbibition and drainage curves are entered with the appropriate saturation functions above. The region keyword IMBNUM is then used to assign imbibition table numbers to cells. The SATOPTS keyword should be used to enable the hysteresis treatment. More details of the hysteresis models can be found under "Hysteresis" in the ECLIPSE Technical Description .
PROPS_HYSTERESIS.name: PROPS_HYSTERESIS

PROPS_OPERATIONAL_KEYWORDS.description: These may be used with keywords that specify arrays over grid cells.
PROPS_OPERATIONAL_KEYWORDS.name: PROPS_OPERATIONAL_KEYWORDS

PROPS_PRESSURE_TABLES.description: Functions of pressure ( ROCK , PVDO , PVTO , PVTW , PVTG ) are entered in a form similar to that of the saturation functions. When multiple tables are entered, these may be associated with cells using the PVTNUM keyword. In addition, DENSITY or GRAVITY keyword data is entered for each pressure table region. An alternative for rock properties is to use the ROCKNUM keyword to specify rock table numb
PROPS_PRESSURE_TABLES.name: PROPS_PRESSURE_TABLES

PROPS_PROPS_SECTION_KEYWORDS.description: A list of all keywords which may occur in the PROPS section grouped by function is given below, together with a brief description of their use. This is followed by an alphabetic list. A more detailed description may be found by looking up the keyword in the manual.
PROPS_PROPS_SECTION_KEYWORDS.name: PROPS_PROPS_SECTION_KEYWORDS

PROPS_ROCK_PRESSURE_TABLES.description: The following methods exist for specifying the change in rock pore volume and transmissibility as a function of pressure.
PROPS_ROCK_PRESSURE_TABLES.name: PROPS_ROCK_PRESSURE_TABLES

PROPS_SATURATION_FUNCTIONS.description: Saturation functions are used to describe properties that depend on the phase saturations, namely the relative permeabilities and capillary pressures.
PROPS_SATURATION_FUNCTIONS.name: PROPS_SATURATION_FUNCTIONS

PROPS_SURFACE_DENSITIES.description: The three possible surface densities are set using the DENSITY keyword. This is required when formation volumes are used, in order to define reservoir densities. For compositional runs, the equation of state defines the hydrocarbon reservoir densities, and only the water value is required. DENSITY always contains three items, even if water is not present in the run.
PROPS_SURFACE_DENSITIES.name: PROPS_SURFACE_DENSITIES

PROPS_TRACER_TRACKING.description: The following keywords can be used in both ECLIPSE 100 and ECLIPSE 300.
PROPS_TRACER_TRACKING.name: PROPS_TRACER_TRACKING

PROPS_WATER_PRESSURE_TABLES.name: PROPS_WATER_PRESSURE_TABLES

A full description of these actions can be found under "Group production rules" in the ECLIPSE Technical Description .
PRORDER.name: PRORDER

The actions may either be performed in the same sequence as specified in record 1 of keyword PRORDER , or in the original sequence given in WLIFT .

REACOPS.description: The REACOPS keywords specifies options used in the chemical reactions model, see "Chemical reactions" in the ECLIPSE Technical Description .

parameter_names: Convergence criteria for the sum of the non-linear residual. The timestep will only be accepted if the non-linear residual is less than this value. The sum of the non-linear residual can be output in the SUMMARY section by including the NLRESSUM keyword. This constraint ensures conservation between reacting components. The constraint can be disabled by specifying a negative value.

Convergence criteria for the maximum element of the non-linear residual. The timestep will only be accepted if the maximum element of the non-linear residual is less than this value. The sum of the non-linear residual can be output in the SUMMARY section by including the NLRESMAX keyword. In a similar manner to the first item, this constraint ensures conservation between reacting components. The constraint can be disabled by specifying a negative value.

Limit the reaction rates such that only reactants present at the start of the timestep can be consumed within the timestep. Note with this simplification a component produced by one reaction cannot be consumed by another until the next timestep. Similarly a reactant flowing into a block cannot be consumed until the next timestep.

Scaling factor to ensure that the reaction rate of zero-order reactants tends to zero as the reactant disappears. In equilibrium deviation reactions (see the EQLDREAC keyword) if a reaction rate is independent of the concentration of a reactant, then the rate is multiplied by a factor m / ( m + s ) where m is the molar density of the reactant and s is given by this item. Please note that the default value is an experimental value and may be adjusted to ensure that the scaling factor m / ( m + s ) tends to zero with the concentration of the reactant.
Choice of model for reaction rate in the water phase.

ROMF.description: This keyword specifies the initial residual oil composition values for each cell. It can only be used with the SOR option. When flashed at the initial cell pressure the fluid must be a single phase oil.
ROMF.name: ROMF

RPTCPL.description: This keyword activates the output of a set of data (see the example output below) which can be used by programs that interface with ECLIPSE. This keyword can also be used as a shortcut to output this data.
RPTCPL.name: RPTCPL

The frequency at which restart files are written ( n in item 1).

RPTGRID.description: The keyword should be followed by a string of mnemonics to request output of grid data to the print file. The appropriate keywords used to input grid data, such as DX and DY , may be used as mnemonics. Aliases may be used; for example DR may be used in place of DX and DTHETA may be used in place of DY . The data should be terminated by a slash (/).
RPTGRID.name: RPTGRID

RPTGRIDL.description: RPTGRIDL is used to request output of GRID section data for local grids. The keyword data is the same as for the first 57 mnemonics described in the RPTGRID keyword, except for the following switches (see also section "RPTGRID - definition with integer controls" in the ECLIPSE Technical Description ):
RPTGRIDL.name: RPTGRIDL

As 1, but the connections between the global and local grids are also written to the Debug file.
As 2, but the connections written to the Debug file have the local grids stacked in the z- direction so that they do not overlay one another.

RPTHMD.description: The keyword should be followed some or all of the following integer items, which control the amount of data written to the HMD file (see "Gradient Option" in the ECLIPSE Technical Description ). Values greater than zero generally reduce the amount of output. The data should be terminated with a slash (/). Repeat counts (for example, 3*0) can be used if required but with no spaces before or after t
RPTHMD.name: RPTHMD

RPTHMG.description: The keyword can be used to switch on or off the output of gradient information to the HMD file for individual groups (see "Gradient Option" in the ECLIPSE Technical Description ). This is normally used by the SimOpt program.
RPTHMG.name: RPTHMG
parameter_names: Group name.
Flag to switch the output for the specified group (or groups) on or off in the gradient HMD file.

RPTHMW.description: The keyword can be used to switch on or off the output of gradient information to the HMD file for individual wells (see "Gradient Option" in the ECLIPSE Technical Description ). This is normally used by the SimOpt program.
RPTHMW.name: RPTHMW
parameter_names: Well name, well name template, well list or well list template

RPTIBFLO.description: This keyword controls whether the interblock flows (both surface and reservoir flows) reported in the restart files are the values at the restart time or an average calculated between the previous restart (or the beginning of the run) and the current restart. The keyword does not alter the calculation of interblock flows used internally in the simulator.
RPTIBFLO.name: RPTIBFLO
parameter_names: The nature of the reported interblock flows:

parameters.brief: DEFAULT: CURRENT
parameters.name: The nature of the reported interblock flows:

RPTINIT.description: The keyword should be followed by a string of mnemonics to request output of GRID and EDIT data to the .INIT (or .FINIT) file. The appropriate keywords used to input some GRID and EDIT data, such as DX and DY , may be used as mnemonics. Aliases may also be used, for instance, DR may be used in place of DX and DTHETA may be used in place of DY .
RPTINIT.name: RPTINIT

RPTISOL.description: This keyword requests ECLIPSE to generate a grid array of isolated reservoir region numbers, which it outputs to the Debug file. The array can then be extracted and included in the input data file under the keyword ISOLNUM , to activate the efficient solution technique for independent reservoir regions (see "Independent reservoir regions" in the ECLIPSE Technical Description ).
RPTISOL.name: RPTISOL

RPTONLY.description: This keyword requests that summary data be written to the Summary file only at report times. The default, if the RPTONLY keyword is not present (and it was not requested in a restart file), is to write the summary information at every timestep.
RPTONLY.name: RPTONLY

RPTONLYO.description: This keyword requests that summary data be written to the Summary file at every timestep. This is the default situation unless overridden in a restart file. This keyword need, therefore, only be used when RPTONLY has previously been used and it is wished to turn off this behavior later in the run.
RPTONLYO.name: RPTONLYO

RPTOPT.description: This keyword is used to request the detail of reporting from the reservoir optimization option. The presence of this keyword is entirely optional.
RPTOPT.name: RPTOPT

RPTPROPS.description: The keyword should be followed by a list of mnemonics which control the output of PROPS section data to the Print file.
RPTPROPS.name: RPTPROPS

RPTREGS.description: The keyword should be followed by a list of mnemonics which control the output of REGIONS section data to the Print file.
RPTREGS.name: RPTREGS

RPTRST.description: The keyword should be followed by a list of mnemonics which control the output of data to the Restart file. The list should be terminated by a slash (/). Note that no restart files will be written if no RPTRST input keywords or mnemonics are specified.
RPTRST.name: RPTRST

RPTRUNSP.description: If this keyword is specified in the RUNSPEC section, a listing of the parameters set in the RUNSPEC section will be written to the Print file. This output includes all variables set in the RUNSPEC section (both default and user- defined values).
RPTRUNSP.name: RPTRUNSP

RPTSCHED.description: The keyword should be followed by a list of mnemonics which control the output of SCHEDULE section data to the Print file. Wherever possible, the mnemonics correspond to the related keywords. The list should be terminated by a slash (/).
RPTSCHED.name: RPTSCHED

RPTSLN.description: The keyword should be followed by a list of mnemonics which control the output of data to the streamline output files. This keyword will not cause streamlines to be traced by ECLIPSE; it will simply cause any streamlines generated for other purposes such as the Lagrangian Tracer Solver ( LAGTRAC ) to be output. The list should be terminated by a slash (/).
RPTSLN.name: RPTSLN

RPTSMRY.description: The keyword should be followed by a single integer which determines whether or not ECLIPSE prints a table of the variables to be written to the Summary file during the current run.
RPTSMRY.name: RPTSMRY

RPTSOL.description: The keyword should be followed by a list of mnemonics which control the output of SOLUTION section data to the Print file. Wherever possible, the mnemonics correspond to the related keywords. The list should be terminated by a slash (/).
RPTSOL.name: RPTSOL

RS.description: The keyword should be followed by one real number for every grid block, specifying the initial solution gas-oil ratio. The data field should be terminated by a slash (/).
RS.name: RS

RSCONST.description: The keyword is used to declare that dead oil contains a constant and uniform concentration of dissolved gas. This provides a more efficient way of modeling black oil systems in which there is no free gas and the pressure never falls below the bubble point. The flags for gas and dissolved gas in the RUNSPEC section should not be switched on (keywords GAS and DISGAS ), so that gas is not treated in
RSCONST.name: RSCONST
parameter_names: The dissolved gas concentration (R s ).
The bubble point pressure.

parameters.brief: UNITS: sm 3 /sm 3 ( METRIC ), Mscf/stb ( FIELD ), scc/scc ( LAB ), sm 3 /sm 3 ( PVT-M )

parameters.brief: The run will terminate if the pressure in any grid block falls below this value.
parameters.name: The bubble point pressure.

RSCONSTT.description: The keyword is used to declare that the dead oil associated with each individual PVT table region contains a constant and uniform concentration of dissolved gas. This provides a more efficient way of modeling black oil systems in which there is no free gas and the pressure never falls below the bubble point.
RSCONSTT.name: RSCONSTT
parameter_names: The dissolved gas concentration (R s ).
The bubble point pressure.

RSGI.description: The data comprises NTPVT (set in the TABDIMS keyword) tables of saturated oil gas-oil ratio multiplier functions, each terminated by a slash (/), describing the variation of the maximum possible GOR of oil with pressure and Gi values. Each table consists of up to NPPVT (set in the TABDIMS keyword) sets of data records. Each set of records within a table consists of up to NPPVT records of data item
RSGI.name: RSGI
parameter_names: The oil pressure value.

The factor by which the saturated oil GOR calculated from the PVTO keyword at a pressure corresponding to item 1 has to be multiplied to give the true saturated oil GOR at a pressure corresponding to item 1 and a Gi value given by item 1 in the corresponding GINODE table.

parameters.brief: The values should increase monotonically down the column.
parameters.name: The oil pressure value.

The factor by which the saturated oil GOR calculated from the PVTO keyword at a pressure corresponding to item 1 has to be multiplied to give the true saturated oil GOR at a pressure corresponding to item 1 and a Gi value given by item 1 in the corresponding GINODE table.

RSM.description: This keyword requests one line per timestep output to the Run Summary file during the run. (It does not affect output to the RSM file due to the RUNSUM item).
RSM.name: RSM

RSSPEC.description: The keyword requests that a Restart Index file should be written at the end of the run. The file contains a list of the arrays written to the Restart file(s) at each restart time. See "File handling in ECLIPSE" in the ECLIPSE Technical Description .
RSSPEC.name: RSSPEC

RSVD.description: The data comprises NTEQUL (see keyword EQLDIMS ) tables of dissolved gas-oil ratio versus depth, one for each equilibration region. Each table consists of 2 columns of data, and must be terminated by a slash (/). Item 7 of the EQUIL keyword must be set to a strictly positive value in order to take into account the RSVD data.
RSVD.name: RSVD
parameter_names: Depth values.
The corresponding values of R s , the dissolved gas-oil ratio.

parameters.brief: The values should increase monotonically down the column.
parameters.name: Depth values.

parameters.name: The corresponding values of R s , the dissolved gas-oil ratio.

RSW.description: This keyword should be used in CO2SOL and/or H2SSOL , or GASSOL cases where the initial solution is given by enumeration.
RSW.name: RSW

RSWVD.description: The data comprises a table of concentrations of dissolved gases (for example, CO 2 and or H 2 S) versus depth. Each table consists of number columns of data (for example, 2 columns for CO2SOL or H2SSOL , 3 columns for CO2SOL and H2SSOL , and NCMPHW +1 columns for the GASSOL case), and must be terminated by a slash (/).

RTEMP.description: When an equation of state (EoS) is being used, the reservoir temperature must be specified. This is then used to calculate reduced temperatures according to the formula T r = T res / T c , where T c is the critical temperature. In Thermal simulations this keyword can be used to set the initial temperature in the reservoir.
RTEMP.name: RTEMP

RTEMPA.description: The RTEMPA keyword is used to specify the initial reservoir temperature in runs where the Temperature option is active (keyword TEMP in the RUNSPEC section).
RTEMPA.name: RTEMPA

RTEMPVD.description: The RTEMPVD keyword is used to specify the initial reservoir temperature as a function of depth, in runs where the Temperature option is active (see keyword TEMP in the RUNSPEC section).
RTEMPVD.name: RTEMPVD
parameter_names: Depth values.
The corresponding values of reservoir temperature.

parameters.brief: The values should increase monotonically down the column.
parameters.name: Depth values.

parameters.brief: UNITS: °C ( METRIC ), °F ( FIELD ), °C ( LAB ), °C ( PVT-M )
parameters.name: The corresponding values of reservoir temperature.

RUNSPEC.description: The RUNSPEC section is the first section of an ECLIPSE data input file. It contains the run title, start date, units, various problem dimensions (numbers of blocks, wells, tables and so forth), flags for phases or components present and option switches. It may be preceded only by comments, global keywords (see "Global keywords" ) and LOAD . The RUNSPEC section must always be present, unless the LO
RUNSPEC.name: RUNSPEC

RUNSUM.description: This keyword requests that the data in the SUMMARY files should be output in a tabulated format in addition to the usual summary files, which are unaffected.
RUNSUM.name: RUNSUM

RV.description: The keyword should be followed by one real number for every grid block, specifying the initial vapor oil-gas ratio. The data field should be terminated by a slash (/).
RV.name: RV

RVCONST.description: The keyword is used to declare that dry gas contains a constant and uniform concentration of vaporized oil. This provides a more efficient way of modeling gas condensate systems in which there is no free oil and the pressure never falls below the dew point. The flags for oil and vaporized oil should not be switched on (keywords OIL and VAPOIL in the RUNSPEC section), so that oil is not treated in
RVCONST.name: RVCONST
parameter_names: The vaporized oil concentration (R v ).
The dew point pressure.

parameters.brief: UNITS: sm 3 /sm 3 ( METRIC ), stb/Mscf ( FIELD ), scc/scc ( LAB ), sm 3 /sm 3 ( PVT-M )
parameters.name: The vaporized oil concentration (R v ).

parameters.brief: DEFAULT: 0.0
parameters.name: The dew point pressure.

RVCONSTT.description: The keyword is used to declare that the dry gas associated with each individual PVT table region contains a constant and uniform concentration of vaporized oil. This provides a more efficient way of modeling gas condensate systems in which there is no free oil and the pressure never falls below the dew point.
RVCONSTT.name: RVCONSTT
parameter_names: The vaporized oil concentration (R v ).
The dew point pressure.

parameters.brief: UNITS: sm 3 /sm 3 ( METRIC ), stb/Mscf ( FIELD ), scc/scc ( LAB ), sm 3 /sm 3 ( PVT-M )
parameters.name: The vaporized oil concentration (R v ).

parameters.brief: DEFAULT: 0.0
parameters.name: The dew point pressure.

RVGI.description: The data comprises NTPVT (set in the TABDIMS keyword) tables of saturated gas oil-gas ratio multiplier functions, each terminated by a slash (/), describing the variation of the maximum possible OGR of gas with pressure and Gi values. Each table consists of up to NPPVT (set in the TABDIMS keyword) sets of data records. Each set of records within a table consists of up to NPPVT records of data item
RVGI.name: RVGI
parameter_names: The gas pressure value.

The factor by which the saturated OGR calculated from the PVTG keyword at a pressure corresponding to item 1 has to be multiplied to give the true saturated OGR at a pressure corresponding to item 1 and a Gi value given by item 1 in the corresponding GINODE table.

parameters.brief: The values should increase monotonically down the column.
parameters.name: The gas pressure value.

The factor by which the saturated OGR calculated from the PVTG keyword at a pressure corresponding to item 1 has to be multiplied to give the true saturated OGR at a pressure corresponding to item 1 and a Gi value given by item 1 in the corresponding GINODE table.

RVVD.description: The data comprises NTEQUL (see keyword EQLDIMS ) tables of vaporized oil-gas ratio versus depth, one for each equilibration region.
RVVD.name: RVVD
parameter_names: Depth values.
The corresponding values of Rv, the vaporized oil-gas ratio.

parameters.brief: The values should increase monotonically down the column.
parameters.name: Depth values.

parameters.name: The corresponding values of Rv, the vaporized oil-gas ratio.

SAKRO.description: The SAKRO keyword specifies the value of oil relative permeability at the maximum oil saturation within each grid block for scaling the oil relative permeability for high concentrations of adsorbed solids.
SAKRO.name: SAKRO

SAKRORW.description: The SAKRORW keyword specifies the value of oil relative permeability at the critical water saturation within each grid block for scaling oil relative permeability to water for high concentrations of adsorbed solids.
SAKRORW.name: SAKRORW

SAKRW.description: The SAKRW keyword specifies the value of water relative permeability at the maximum water saturation within each grid block for scaling the water relative permeability for high concentrations of adsorbed solids.
SAKRW.name: SAKRW

SAKRWR.description: The SAKRWR keyword specifies the value of water relative permeability at the critical oil to water saturation within each grid block for scaling the water relative permeability for high concentrations of adsorbed solids.
SAKRWR.name: SAKRWR

SALINITR.description: This keyword is an extension of the SALINITY keyword and can be used to specify a salinity value region-by-region . The regions are the regions defined for the EoS (Equation Of State) using EOSNUM and their number is specified in NMEOSR in keyword TABDIMS .
SALINITR.name: SALINITR

SALINITY.description: This keyword can be used to define the salinity used in the modified Peng-Robinson equation of state in GASWAT cases and in the default CO 2 solubility data in CO2SOL cases.
SALINITY.name: SALINITY

SALT.description: The keyword should be followed by one real number for every grid block specifying the initial salt concentration. The data field should be terminated by a slash (/).
SALT.name: SALT

SALTEFF.description: This keyword may only be used when salinity dependent surfactant and/or polymer models are active (when keywords SURFSTES with ESSNODE or PLYVISCS with ESPNODE are specified in the PROPS section).
SALTEFF.name: SALTEFF

SALTNODE.description: The data comprises NTPVT (set in the TABDIMS keyword) tables of salt concentration values, each terminated by a slash (/), describing the nodal values for salt concentration to be used in the calculation of the polymer solution viscosity.
SALTNODE.name: SALTNODE

SALTREST.description: This keyword defines the salt concentration value for the reservoir for restart runs where the base run water properties were specified with no salinity dependence, for example when specified using the PVTW keyword. This allows you to introduce salinity dependent water properties on restart, using, for example, PVTWSALT with LOWSALT or BRINE .
SALTREST.name: SALTREST

SALTVD.description: The data comprises NTEQUL (see keyword EQLDIMS ) tables of salt concentration versus depth, one for each equilibration region. The Brine option must be activated (keyword BRINE ).
SALTVD.name: SALTVD
parameter_names: Depth values.
to [N+1] The corresponding values of salt concentration.

parameters.brief: The values should increase monotonically down the column.
parameters.name: Depth values.

parameters.brief: The standard Brine Model has a single salt component. In this case, column 2 of this keyword contains a single value which is the concentrat
parameters.name: to [N+1] The corresponding values of salt concentration.

SAMG.description: ECLIPSE 300. This is an optional keyword which specifies that the underlying linear systems should be solved using the algebraic multigrid solver SAMG, and controls its behavior. SAMG is currently a suitable choice in combination with the IMPES keyword, but not in general for other types of simulation. Some additional SAMG control parameters are included under the CVCRIT keyword.
SAMG.name: SAMG
parameter_names: EPS
REUSE

parameters.brief: This defines the tolerance used in the stopping criterion. Positive values define the required relative residual norm reduction. Negative va
parameters.name: EPS

parameters.brief: Specifies whether to reuse the coarse grid and smoothing operators from a previous call to SAMG .
parameters.name: REUSE

SAPCW.description: The SAPCW keyword specifies the maximum value of oil-water capillary pressure for scaling the capillary pressure saturation tables for high concentrations of adsorbed solids.
SAPCW.name: SAPCW

SASGL.description: The SASGL keyword specifies the connate gas saturation (that is, the smallest gas saturation in a gas saturation function table) within each grid block for scaling the oil and water relative permeabilities for high concentrations of adsorbed solids.
SASGL.name: SASGL

SASOWCR.description: The SASOWCR keyword specifies the critical oil in water saturation (that is, the largest oil saturation for which the oil relative permeability to water is zero) within each grid block for scaling the oil relative permeability to water for high concentrations of adsorbed solids.
SASOWCR.name: SASOWCR

SASWCR.description: The SASWCR keyword specifies the critical water saturation (that is, the largest water saturation for which the water relative permeability is zero) within each grid block for scaling the water relative permeability for high concentrations of adsorbed solids.
SASWCR.name: SASWCR

SASWL.description: The SASWL keyword specifies the connate water saturation (that is, the smallest water saturation in a water saturation function table) within each grid block for scaling the oil relative permeability to water and gas for high concentrations of adsorbed solids.
SASWL.name: SASWL

SASWU.description: The SASWU keyword specifies the maximum water saturation (that is, the highest water saturation in a water saturation function table) within each grid block for scaling the water relative permeability for high concentrations of adsorbed solids.
SASWU.name: SASWU

SATNUM.description: The keyword should be followed by one integer for every grid block in the current input box specifying the saturation function region to which it belongs. The region number should not be less than 1 or greater than NTSFUN (set in the TABDIMS keyword). The data must be terminated by a slash (/).
SATNUM.name: SATNUM

SATOPTS.description: The keyword enables the use of a directional, irreversible or hysteretic relative permeability model and an option to allow capillary pressures to depend on surface tensions. The keyword should be followed by some or all of the following options. The default is for all these options to be switched off.
SATOPTS.name: SATOPTS

SAVE.description: The SAVE keyword in the RUNSPEC section is used to write a SAVE file containing the initial non-recurrent data. In ECLIPSE 300, SAVE file output can be controlled using the MULTSAVE keyword.
SAVE.name: SAVE

SAVEEND.description: This keyword requests that a SAVE file record is always written at the end of the run, irrespective of the reason for ending.
SAVEEND.name: SAVEEND

SCALECRS.description: The SCALECRS keyword is optional in runs with the end-point scaling option active (keyword ENDSCALE in the RUNSPEC section). It is used to control the scaling method.
SCALECRS.name: SCALECRS

SCALELIM.description: The data comprises NTENDP (see item 3 of keyword ENDSCALE in the RUNSPEC section) records of saturation scaling limits to be used in the end point versus depth table method of defining saturation table end point scaling data. Each record consists of at most one real number terminated by a slash (/).
SCALELIM.name: SCALELIM

SCDATAB.description: This keyword may be used to input tables which give the reduction factor for the PI of each connection in a well as a function of the current amount of scale deposited per unit length of perforated interval. The tables defined here are allocated to individual wells with the WSCTAB keyword. The rate of scale deposition around the well connections per unit water flow rate should be defined as a func
SCDATAB.name: SCDATAB

SCHEDULE.description: The SCHEDULE section specifies the operations to be simulated (production and injection controls and constraints) and the times at which output reports are required. Vertical flow performance curves and simulator tuning parameters may also be specified in the SCHEDULE section.

SCHEDULE_DEFINE_SEPARATORS.description: The separator conditions associated with a well define the splitting of the well production in to stock tank oil and gas.
SCHEDULE_DEFINE_SEPARATORS.name: SCHEDULE_DEFINE_SEPARATORS

SCHEDULE_FLASH_TRANSFORMATION_AND_SEPARA.description: The keyword can be used firstly to define the initial separator conditions, and subsequently to change them. When the separator conditions have been changed, ECLIPSE will transform the oil and gas flow rates of the wells and groups that feed into the separator.
SCHEDULE_FLASH_TRANSFORMATION_AND_SEPARA.name: SCHEDULE_FLASH_TRANSFORMATION_AND_SEPARATOR_CONDITIONS

SCHEDULE_SALES_GAS_CONTROL.description: This facility provides a means of controlling the export of associated gas from an oil field, which may at the same time have controls on the oil production rate. The gas export rate is controlled by reinjecting the surplus gas not required for sale.
SCHEDULE_SALES_GAS_CONTROL.name: SCHEDULE_SALES_GAS_CONTROL

SCHEDULE_SATELLITE_GROUP_FLOWS.description: Satellite groups can be used to incorporate known production and injection flows from outside the simulation grid. They are groups that contain no wells or subordinate groups, and whose production and injection rates may be set periodically with the following keywords.
SCHEDULE_SATELLITE_GROUP_FLOWS.name: SCHEDULE_SATELLITE_GROUP_FLOWS

SDENSITY.description: The data comprises NTPVT (set in the TABDIMS keyword) records, each terminated by a slash (/). Each record consists of a single item of data, defining the surface density of the miscible injection gas.

SHRATE.description: This keyword is used to activate the shear rate form of the alternative (natural logarithm-based) polymer shear thinning/thickening option and to supply the required shear rate constant. This keyword can only be used in conjunction with keyword PLYSHLOG .
SHRATE.name: SHRATE

SIGMA.description: If the dual porosity or dual permeability options are being used (by specifying the DUALPORO or DUALPERM keyword in the RUNSPEC section), this keyword can be used to specify a multiplier to be used in the construction of the matrix-fracture coupling transmissibilities.
SIGMA.name: SIGMA

SIGMAGD.description: This keyword can be used to specify an alternative matrix-fracture coupling for matrix cells in which the production mechanism is gravity drainage due to the presence of gas in the fractures.
SIGMAGD.name: SIGMAGD

SIGMAGDV.description: This keyword can be used to specify an alternative matrix-fracture coupling for matrix cells in which the production mechanism is gravity drainage due to the presence of gas in the fractures.
SIGMAGDV.name: SIGMAGDV

SIGMATH.description: This keyword can only be used with the THERMAL option (keyword THERMAL in the RUNSPEC section).
SIGMATH.name: SIGMATH

SIGMAV.description: If the dual porosity option is being used (keyword DUALPORO in the RUNSPEC section), this keyword can be used to specify a multiplier to be applied in the construction of the matrix-fracture coupling transmissibilities.
SIGMAV.name: SIGMAV

SIMULATE.description: This keyword counteracts a NOSIM keyword in the SCHEDULE section and turns on the timestep simulation.
SIMULATE.name: SIMULATE

SKIP.description: This keyword causes all subsequent keywords to be ignored, up to the next ENDSKIP keyword.
SKIP.name: SKIP

SKIP100.description: This keyword causes ECLIPSE 100 to ignore all subsequent keywords, up to the next ENDSKIP keyword. This keyword has no effect in ECLIPSE 300 simulation runs.
SKIP100.name: SKIP100

SKIP300.description: This keyword causes ECLIPSE 300 to ignore all subsequent keywords, up to the next ENDSKIP keyword. This keyword is has no effect in ECLIPSE 100 simulation runs.
SKIP300.name: SKIP300

SKIPREST.description: The SKIPREST keyword has no associated data. It instructs ECLIPSE to skip the subsequent keywords in the SCHEDULE section of a restart run until the restart time has been reached. This saves you from having to delete the keywords yourself. It should normally be placed at the very start of the SCHEDULE section - in ECLIPSE 100 parallel runs it is strongly recommended that the keyword is the first o
SKIPREST.name: SKIPREST

SKIPSTAB.description: This keyword requests the fast flash option which can be used in EoS compositional runs. See "Fast flash option" in the ECLIPSE Technical Description .
SKIPSTAB.name: SKIPSTAB

SKRO.description: The SKRO keyword specifies the value of oil relative permeability at the maximum oil saturation within each grid block for scaling the surfactant oil relative permeability.
SKRO.name: SKRO

SKRORG.description: The SKRORG keyword specifies the value of oil relative permeability at the critical gas saturation within each grid block for scaling the surfactant oil relative permeability to gas.
SKRORG.name: SKRORG

SKRORW.description: The SKRORW keyword specifies the value of oil relative permeability at the critical water saturation within each grid block for scaling the surfactant oil relative permeability to water.
SKRORW.name: SKRORW

SKRW.description: The SKRW keyword specifies the value of water relative permeability at the maximum water saturation within each grid block for scaling the surfactant water relative permeability.
SKRW.name: SKRW

SKRWR.description: This keyword is available in both ECLIPSE simulators.
SKRWR.name: SKRWR

ECLIPSE starts their simulation processes, which waits for further instructions from the master run. (See "Reservoir coupling" in the ECLIPSE Technical Description .)

parameter_names: See "Initial fluid in place" . For ECLIPSE Compositional fluid in place, quantities are calculated relative to a user defined separator chain and the total number of moles of each hydrocarbon component within the volume in question. For fluids within a particular reservoir phase (for example the FOIPL keyword), the volume is calculated using the total number of moles of each hydrocarbon component within the volume and phase in question. Users should remember that some of the simple relationships which hold true for black oil simulations such as FOIP = FOIPL + FOIPV do not apply to compositional simulations. The reason for this is: compositional variation between reservoir vapor and reservoir liquid, compositional variation between regions, and differing separator chains in some cases.
See “Format of SUMMARY keywords with a component index” .

UNIFIN.name: UNIFIN

UNIFOUT.description: This indicates that output files (for example Restart and Summary files), which may be either multiple or unified, are to be unified. That is, instead of producing separate Restart and Summary files for each report step, these files are amalgamated into a single file of each type. The default is for multiple (non-unified) files.

UNIFOUTS.description: This indicates that summary output files that may be either multiple or unified, are to be unified. This keyword overwrites the behavior of the MULTOUT keyword, which acts on both summary and restart files.
UNIFOUTS.name: UNIFOUTS

UNIFSAVE.description: This indicates that ECLIPSE 300 Save files, which may be either multiple or unified, are to be unified. The default is multiple.

VDFLOW.description: This keyword enables the treatment of non-Darcy effects in inter-block flow, and specifies the non-Darcy flow coefficient. This is commonly known as β , the non-Darcy flow coefficient, and is entered in units of atma.s 2 .g -1 (the Forchheimer) in all unit sets. Dake (1978) shows a typical value of β = 10 7 cm - 1 , which is 9.86 Forchheimer units.
VDFLOW.name: VDFLOW

VDFLOWR.description: This keyword is an alternative to VDFLOW allowing input of the non-Darcy flow coefficient on a region-by-region basis. The data comprises NTSFUN (set in the TABDIMS keyword) records, each containing a single data item terminated with a slash(/).
VDFLOWR.name: VDFLOWR
parameter_names: The non-Darcy flow coefficient. This is commonly known as β , the non-Darcy flow coefficient, and is entered in units of atma.s 2 .g -1 (the Forchheimer) in all unit sets. Dake (1978) in chapter 8 shows a typical value of β = 10 7 cm - 1 , which is 9.86 Forchheimer units.

WCYCLE.description: This keyword provides a means of automatically cycling wells on and off for specified intervals of time. The facility can be used, for example, to simulate a WAG process, where the injection well is represented by separate water and gas injectors that are cycled on and off alternately.
